The character is polite to strangers but cruel to people who depend on him. — その登場人物は見知らぬ人には礼儀正しいが、自分を頼りにしている人には冷酷だ。
In a cruel twist of fate, the one person who could confirm her story had left the country the day before. — 運命はむごいもので、彼女の話を裏づけられる唯一の人物は前日に国外へ出ていた。
The criticism was relentless, and some of the remarks about her appearance were downright cruel. — 批判が絶えず続き、彼女の外見をあげつらう発言には、あまりにひどいものもあった。

usage.register: Somewhat literary. Often describes a person’s habitual manner, facial expression, or lack of visible reaction.

en: showing little emotion or excitement, often with an impression of dullness or unresponsiveness
ja: 感情をほとんど表に出さない、反応の乏しい、無表情な

nuance.ja: 驚いたり喜んだりする場面でも顔つきや態度がほとんど変わらず、周囲からは鈍い、取りつく島がないと見えることがある。a stolid expression は、話しかけても表情がほとんど動かない様子。文脈によっては、どっしりして動じないという描写にもなる。
nuance.en: Stolid describes a person or manner that shows little outward reaction. It can make someone seem dull or hard to engage, although in some contexts it suggests a solid, unflappable presence.

en: stoic: Often suggests enduring pain or hardship without complaint. Stolid describes little outward reaction and can suggest dullness.
impassive: Describes a face or manner that reveals no emotion, often in a particular moment. Stolid can also characterize someone’s usual manner.
phlegmatic: Describes a temperament that is calm and slow to become excited or upset. Stolid can convey an impression of dullness as well.
ja: stoic：苦痛や逆境を顔に出さず、黙って耐える姿勢を表しやすい。stolid は外から見える反応の乏しさや鈍さを描く。
impassive：その場の表情や態度に感情が出ないこと。stolid は普段から反応が乏しい人柄にも使える。
phlegmatic：興奮したり動揺したりしにくい落ち着いた気質。stolid は反応が鈍い印象も帯びる。

note.ja: 表情や態度に感情が出ない。
note.en: Showing no outward emotion.

etymology.ja: ラテン語 stolidus「鈍い、愚かな」にさかのぼる。英語への入り方には、フランス語 stolide を経た説と、stolidity「鈍さ、無感動」から作られたとする説がある。
etymology.en: Ultimately from Latin stolidus, ‘dull’ or ‘foolish.’ English may have borrowed it from French stolide or formed it from stolidity.

en: a stolid expression
a stolid manner
remain stolid
sit stolidly
ja: a stolid expression — ほとんど感情の出ない表情
a stolid manner — 反応の乏しい態度
remain stolid — 表情をほとんど変えない
sit stolidly — 感情を表に出さず座っている

en: Everyone else laughed, but he sat there stolidly, his expression unchanged.
The guard listened with a stolid expression and then asked to see our passes.
Her usually stolid uncle broke into a grin when he saw the puppy.
The narrator’s stolid manner makes even the wildest events sound ordinary.
ja: Everyone else laughed, but he sat there stolidly, his expression unchanged. — ほかのみんなは笑ったが、彼は表情を変えずに座っていた。
The guard listened with a stolid expression and then asked to see our passes. — 警備員はほとんど表情を変えずに話を聞き、それから通行証を見せるよう求めた。
Her usually stolid uncle broke into a grin when he saw the puppy. — 普段は感情をあまり顔に出さない叔父が、子犬を見るとにっこり笑った。
The narrator’s stolid manner makes even the wildest events sound ordinary. — 語り手の反応があまりに淡々としていて、とんでもない出来事までありふれた話に聞こえる。

usage.tone: A strong expression of criticism or outrage. Use a travesty of justice or a travesty of the original to identify what was distorted.

en: a grossly distorted or inadequate version of what something should be
a burlesque or grotesquely exaggerated imitation, especially in literature
ja: 本来の姿をひどくゆがめたもの、名ばかりのひどい代物
（文学など）原作を滑稽に仕立て直した作品、戯作

nuance.ja: 公正さや原作への忠実さなど、当然期待されるものがひどく損なわれたと非難する語。a travesty of justice は、不公正な審理や判断を「正義を踏みにじるもの」と強く非難する表現。a travesty of the original は、原作の持ち味を大きく損ねた翻案にも使える。
nuance.en: Travesty condemns something for badly distorting or falling short of a standard it claims to represent. A travesty of justice can be a gravely unfair process or outcome. A travesty of the original can be an adaptation that badly distorts the source.

en: tragedy: Emphasizes suffering or terrible loss. Travesty emphasizes distortion or a serious failure to live up to a standard.
parody: An imitation often intended to amuse or satirize. Travesty can express outrage about an actual process or outcome.
sham: Emphasizes a false appearance of genuineness, as in a sham consultation. Travesty emphasizes how badly the process departs from the ideal.
miscarriage of justice: A more specific expression for a serious failure of justice, often a wrongful conviction. Travesty of justice is strongly evaluative.
ja: tragedy：大きな苦しみや喪失を伴う「悲劇」。travesty は、本来の姿や基準がひどく損なわれたことに焦点がある。
parody：笑いや風刺を狙った模倣。travesty は、実際の手続や結果に対する強い非難にも使える。
sham：a sham consultation のように、実質を伴わず形だけであることを強調する。travesty は、建前と実態のひどい隔たりに焦点がある。
miscarriage of justice：冤罪など、司法が公正な結果を出せなかった重大な事態を指す。travesty of justice は強い非難を込めた表現。

note.ja: a mockery of justice なら、公正さを台無しにするような手続や結果。
note.en: A mockery of justice likewise condemns a process or outcome that undermines justice.

etymology.ja: フランス語 travesti「変装した」を経て、イタリア語 travestire「変装させる、衣装を替える」にさかのぼる。英語では当初、まじめな作品を滑稽に仕立て直したものを指した。
etymology.en: From French travesti, ‘disguised,’ ultimately from Italian travestire, ‘to disguise.’ An early English sense was a comic recasting of a serious literary work.

en: a travesty of justice
a travesty of the original
an absolute travesty
condemn the outcome as a travesty
ja: a travesty of justice — 正義を踏みにじるような不公正
a travesty of the original — 原作をひどくゆがめたもの
an absolute travesty — まったくひどい代物
condemn the outcome as a travesty — 結果をひどいものだと強く非難する

en: The defense called the proceedings a travesty of justice after its witnesses were barred from testifying.
The critic called the adaptation a travesty of the original novel because it turned its quiet ending into a drawn-out spectacle.
The vote was a travesty. Half the members never even received a ballot.
The play is a deliberate travesty of a solemn medieval legend, recast as a quarrel over a missing goat.
ja: The defense called the proceedings a travesty of justice after its witnesses were barred from testifying. — 証人の証言が認められなかったことを受け、弁護側はこの審理を正義を踏みにじるものだと非難した。
The critic called the adaptation a travesty of the original novel because it turned its quiet ending into a drawn-out spectacle. — 静かな結末を延々と続く見せ場に変えてしまったため、批評家はその翻案を原作をひどくゆがめたものと評した。
The vote was a travesty. Half the members never even received a ballot. — あの投票はひどいものだった。構成員の半数には投票用紙すら届いていなかった。
The play is a deliberate travesty of a solemn medieval legend, recast as a quarrel over a missing goat. — その戯曲は、荘重な中世の伝説を、いなくなったヤギをめぐる口論にわざと仕立て直した戯作だ。

usage.spelling: Double the final n in shunned and shunning.
usage.object: Common objects include publicity, the spotlight, and the names of people or groups.

en: to deliberately keep away from a person, place, or activity
to refuse to associate with or acknowledge someone
ja: （人・場所・活動などを）意識して避ける、遠ざける
（人との）付き合いを避ける、仲間外れにする

nuance.ja: 単に接触を避けるだけでなく、関わりを持たないよう意識して距離を置く響きがある。shun publicity は、注目されることを好まず取材などを避けること。be shunned by former friends なら、かつての友人たちから付き合いを避けられるという、拒絶の含みが出る。人以外を目的語に取ると、自分の方針や好みで避けることも表せる。
nuance.en: Shun presents avoidance as a deliberate choice to keep one’s distance. A writer who shuns publicity may turn down interviews and public appearances. Someone shunned by former friends experiences social rejection. With things or activities, the verb can also express a personal preference or policy.

en: avoid: The general verb for keeping away from something or preventing an outcome. Avoid a delay is routine, while shun publicity suggests a deliberate stance toward public attention.
eschew: A formal verb often used of consciously avoiding a practice, style, or habit, as in eschew jargon.
ostracize: Focuses on exclusion from a group or community. Shun also fits an individual avoiding publicity or social events.
steer clear of: A conversational expression for staying away from someone or something, often as a precaution.
ja: avoid：何かに近づかない、望ましくない結果を防ぐなどに広く使う。avoid a delay は「遅れを防ぐ」。shun publicity には、世間の注目から意識的に距離を置く姿勢が出る。
eschew：専門用語や特定の習慣などを意識して避ける、改まった語。eschew jargon は「専門用語を使わないようにする」。
ostracize：集団や共同体から締め出すことに焦点がある。shun は個人が人前に出ることや社交行事を避ける場合にも使う。
steer clear of：用心して人や物に近づかない、という会話表現。

note.ja: 避ける、近づかない。
note.en: Stay away from someone or something.

note.ja: 人を集団から排除する用法で近い。
note.en: Close in the sense of socially excluding someone.

etymology.ja: 古英語 scunian「避ける、嫌う」に由来する。それ以前の語源は不明とされる。
etymology.en: From Old English scunian, meaning to avoid or abhor. Its earlier origin is uncertain.

en: shun publicity
shun the spotlight
shun social gatherings
be shunned by former friends
ja: shun publicity — 世間の注目を避ける
shun the spotlight — 表舞台に出ることを避ける
shun social gatherings — 社交の集まりを避ける
be shunned by former friends — かつての友人たちから避けられる

en: The novelist shuns publicity and rarely gives interviews.
She shuns large industry receptions but enjoys meeting colleagues in small groups.
He found himself shunned by former friends after he spoke out against the club’s leadership.
The fund has long shunned companies that rely on a single customer.
ja: The novelist shuns publicity and rarely gives interviews. — その小説家は世間の注目を避け、めったに取材を受けない。
She shuns large industry receptions but enjoys meeting colleagues in small groups. — 彼女は業界の大きなレセプションには足を運ばないが、少人数で同業者と会うのは好きだ。
He found himself shunned by former friends after he spoke out against the club’s leadership. — クラブの運営陣を公然と批判したあと、彼はかつての友人たちから付き合いを避けられるようになった。
The fund has long shunned companies that rely on a single customer. — そのファンドは以前から、一社の顧客に依存する企業への投資を避けてきた。

usage.praise: For introduces a reason for praise. On can introduce an achievement or quality being praised.
usage.recommendation: Commend something to someone is a formal recommendation. Something that has much to commend it has many merits.

en: to praise someone or something, often formally or publicly
to recommend something as worthy of attention or consideration
to entrust someone or something to another’s care, especially in formal or religious language
ja: （人・行為などを）称賛する、評価する
（案・資料などを）勧める、検討に付す
（人などを人の世話や神の御手に）委ねる

nuance.ja: commend someone for ... は、行動や功績を評価して称賛する。委員会の報告や公式な謝辞などに合う。commend a proposal to the board は、理事会に提案を勧めたり、検討を促したりする改まった言い方。The proposal has much to commend it. なら「その提案には評価できる点が多い」。人を人の世話に委ねる用法は、古風・儀礼的な文脈で見られる。
nuance.en: Commend someone for something expresses approval of an action or achievement, often in a formal statement. To commend a proposal to a board is to recommend it for consideration. A proposal that has much to commend it has several merits. The sense of entrusting someone to another’s care is chiefly formal or ceremonial.

en: praise: The broad verb for expressing approval. Commend often sounds more formal or official.
recommend: The usual everyday choice for suggesting a book, service, or course of action. Commend something to someone is more formal.
congratulate: Expresses pleasure at someone’s success or good fortune. Commend can praise someone’s response to a setback.
command: Pronounced with a different stressed vowel and commonly means to order. Commend has the vowel /e/ and commonly means to praise.
ja: praise：褒めることを幅広く表す。commend は公式に功績を認めるような、改まった響きが出やすい。
recommend：本やサービス、行動などを勧める一般的な語。commend something to someone はより改まった言い方。
congratulate：成功や幸運を祝う。commend は、失敗にどう対応したかを評価する場合にも使える。
command：強勢のある母音が異なり、主に「命じる」。commend は /e/ で、主な意味は「称賛する」。

note.ja: 称賛する、褒める。
note.en: Express approval of someone or something.

note.ja: 検討する価値があるとして勧める。
note.en: Put forward as worthy of consideration.

etymology.ja: ラテン語 commendāre「委ねる、推薦する」にさかのぼる。「相手に託す」ことと、「相手の注意や好意に値するものとして勧める」ことが、この語の用法につながる。recommend と同系。
etymology.en: Ultimately from Latin commendāre, meaning to entrust or recommend. The English senses of entrusting and recommending reflect those older uses. Compare recommend.

en: commend someone for their honesty
be highly commended
commend a report to readers
have much to commend it
commend someone to God’s care
ja: commend someone for their honesty — 人の誠実さを称賛する
be highly commended — 高く評価される
commend a report to readers — 報告書を読者に勧める
have much to commend it — 評価できる点が多い
commend someone to God’s care — 人を神の御手に委ねる

en: The committee commended the team for making the data available to the public.
I commend you for acknowledging the error so promptly.
I commend this report to anyone who wants to understand how the proposal would work in practice.
The proposal has much to commend it, especially its clear division of responsibilities.
At the end of the service, the minister commended the deceased to God’s care.
ja: The committee commended the team for making the data available to the public. — 委員会は、データを一般公開したことについてチームを称賛した。
I commend you for acknowledging the error so promptly. — 誤りをすぐに認めたことは、評価に値します。
I commend this report to anyone who wants to understand how the proposal would work in practice. — 提案が実際にどう機能するか知りたい方には、この報告書をお勧めします。
The proposal has much to commend it, especially its clear division of responsibilities. — その提案には評価できる点が多い。とくに、責任分担が明確だ。
At the end of the service, the minister commended the deceased to God’s care. — 式の終わりに、牧師は故人を神の御手に委ねた。

patterns: It was commendable of someone to do something

usage.register: Often used in considered or formal praise. It commonly describes an effort, decision, quality, or action.

en: deserving praise or approval, especially for the effort, care, or judgment shown
ja: 称賛に値する、評価すべき、立派な

nuance.ja: 行動や姿勢のどこが評価に値するかを示す、やや改まったほめ言葉。a commendable effort は、たとえば企画が目標を達成しなかったとしても、粘り強く取り組んだ努力を評価する言い方。commendable transparency なら、経緯や問題点を率直に明らかにした姿勢への評価。
nuance.en: Commendable often expresses measured approval of a specific action or quality. A commendable effort can fall short of its goal and still deserve praise. Commendable transparency praises the way someone openly explains what happened or what went wrong.

en: commend: The verb describes the act of praising. The panel commended her honesty and Her honesty was commendable express closely related judgments.
admirable: Also means deserving praise and often conveys personal admiration, as in admirable courage.
impressive: Highlights the strong impression that an achievement, ability, or scale makes. Commendable highlights the merit of the effort or conduct.
recommendable: Means worthy of being recommended to others. Commendable means worthy of praise.
ja: commend：称賛するという行為を表す動詞。The panel commended her honesty. と Her honesty was commendable. は、どちらも彼女の誠実さを評価している。
admirable：同じく「称賛に値する」。admirable courage のように、感心や敬意が感じられやすい。
impressive：成果、能力、規模などが強い印象を与えること。commendable は努力や行動が評価に値することに焦点がある。
recommendable：人に勧める価値がある。commendable は「称賛に値する」。

note.ja: 称賛するだけの価値がある。
note.en: Deserving praise.

note.ja: 目的や努力などが称賛に値する、改まった表現。
note.en: A formal near-synonym, often applied to aims or efforts.

etymology.ja: commend「称賛する、勧める」と形容詞を作る -able が対応する。ラテン語 commendāre「委ねる、推薦する」と同系で、現代英語では「称賛できるだけの価値がある」と覚えられる。
etymology.en: Related to commend, ultimately from Latin commendāre, ‘to entrust or recommend.’ In modern English the ending -able makes the sense transparent: worthy of being commended.

en: a commendable effort
commendable restraint
a commendable initiative
commendable transparency
commendably candid
ja: a commendable effort — 称賛に値する努力
commendable restraint — 評価すべき自制
a commendable initiative — 評価に値する取り組み
commendable transparency — 評価すべき透明性
commendably candid — 率直で評価できる

en: The pilot fell short of its target, but the team made a commendable effort to involve the people who would actually use the service.
It was commendable of her to flag the error before anyone else noticed it.
The report is commendably candid about the gaps in the evidence.
The examiner showed commendable restraint in limiting the objection to the claims affected by the amendment.
ja: The pilot fell short of its target, but the team made a commendable effort to involve the people who would actually use the service. — 試験導入は目標に届かなかったが、実際にサービスを使う人たちに参加してもらおうとしたチームの努力は評価に値する。
It was commendable of her to flag the error before anyone else noticed it. — 誰かが気づく前に、彼女が自分から誤りを指摘したのは立派だった。
The report is commendably candid about the gaps in the evidence. — その報告書は、証拠が足りない点を率直に認めており、その姿勢は評価できる。
The examiner showed commendable restraint in limiting the objection to the claims affected by the amendment. — 審査官が異議の対象を補正の影響を受けた請求項に限ったのは、節度ある対応として評価できる。

patterns: go from + adjective + to downright + adjective

usage.adverb: Before an adjective, downright intensifies a judgment, as in downright rude or downright funny.
usage.adjective: Before a noun, it means out-and-out or complete, as in a downright lie.

en: used to emphasize a strong judgment, especially a negative one
complete or unmistakable, used before a noun for emphasis
ja: （副詞）実に、まったく、どう見ても
（形容詞）まったくの、正真正銘の

nuance.ja: 評価を強めて「はっきりそう言える」と言い切る語。downright rude なら「まったく失礼だ」、a downright lie なら「まったくのうそだ」。否定的な評価でよく使うが、downright funny や downright charming のように、意外なほど面白い、すっかり魅力に引き込まれた、という強調にも使える。
nuance.en: Downright makes an assessment emphatic and direct. Downright rude calls the behavior unequivocally rude, and a downright lie leaves little room for a charitable reading. Negative judgments are common, but positive uses such as downright funny or downright charming can convey surprise or enthusiasm.

en: very: Intensifies a degree in a neutral way. Downright often sounds like the speaker is making a firm judgment.
outright: Overlaps in an outright lie. It also describes actions or results without qualification, as in reject a proposal outright or win outright.
utterly: A strong adverb used before adjectives. The adjective utter can modify a noun, as in utter nonsense.
simply: Can mean merely or in a simple way. As an intensifier in simply wonderful it expresses praise, while downright often adds a more forceful or pointed tone.
ja: very：程度を強める一般的な語。downright は、話し手がはっきり評価を下す響きが出やすい。
outright：an outright lie では意味が近い。reject a proposal outright「提案をきっぱり拒絶する」、win outright「単独で勝つ」のように、行為や結果にも使う。
utterly：形容詞を強く修飾する副詞。名詞を修飾するときは utter nonsense のように形容詞 utter を使う。
simply：「単に」「簡潔に」のほか、simply wonderful のような強調にも使う。downright は、より勢いよく断言する響きが出やすい。

note.ja: 「まったく」と形容詞を強める副詞。
note.en: An adverb emphasizing the full force of an adjective.

note.ja: 「まったくの」と名詞を強める形容詞。
note.en: An adjective meaning complete or unmistakable.

etymology.ja: down と right から成り、中英語では「真下へ、垂直に」を表した。そこから早い時期に「すっかり、まったく」という強調の意味でも使われるようになった。
etymology.en: From down and right. In Middle English it could mean ‘straight down.’ The emphatic sense ‘completely’ is also attested from an early period.

usage.register: Formal. Often used of opponents, hostility, or opposition that cannot be softened by persuasion or concessions.

en: impossible to appease or persuade to soften a hostile or opposed attitude
unyielding in opposition or determination
ja: （敵意・反対などが）和らげようのない、何をしても態度を軟化させない
（反対・決意などが）断固として揺るがない

nuance.ja: 説得や譲歩を重ねても、反対や敵意が和らぐ見込みがないという強い表現。an implacable opponent of the merger なら、条件を変えても合併への反対を崩さない相手。人に加えて implacable hostility のように態度そのものも形容できる。
nuance.en: Implacable suggests that persuasion, apologies, or concessions will do little to soften someone’s stance. An implacable opponent of a merger is likely to oppose it even if its terms change. The adjective can also describe the attitude itself, as in implacable hostility.

en: relentless: Highlights pressure or effort that continues without easing. Relentless criticism keeps coming. Implacable opposition is hard to soften or overcome.
ruthless: Highlights willingness to act without mercy or concern for others. Implacable focuses on a stance or feeling that cannot be softened.
adamant: Common for insisting on a particular decision or claim. Implacable is more formal and often suggests a deeply entrenched attitude.
ja: relentless：圧力や努力が勢いを保って続くこと。relentless criticism は絶え間ない批判、implacable opposition は説得しても和らがない反対。
ruthless：他人への同情や手加減を示さないこと。implacable は、相手が働きかけても態度や感情が和らがないことに焦点がある。
adamant：特定の決定や主張を譲らないときによく使う。implacable はより改まった語で、反対や敵意が根深い響きが出やすい。

note.ja: なだめようのない。怒りや敵意について近い。
note.en: Impossible to appease, especially of anger or hostility.

note.ja: 圧力を受けても譲らない。
note.en: Refusing to yield under pressure.

etymology.ja: 古フランス語 implacable を経て、ラテン語 implacābilis「なだめようのない」にさかのぼる。否定の im- と placābilis「なだめることができる」から成り、英語の placate「なだめる」と同系。
etymology.en: From Old French implacable, ultimately from Latin implacābilis, formed from the negative prefix im- and placābilis, ‘able to be appeased.’ Compare placate, ‘to soothe or appease.’

en: Even after the board revised the terms, she remained an implacable opponent of the merger.

ja: Even after the board revised the terms, she remained an implacable opponent of the merger. — 取締役会が条件を見直したあとも、彼女は合併への反対を崩さなかった。
The plan met with implacable opposition from residents who had already rejected two compromises. — その計画は、すでに二つの妥協案を退けていた住民の強硬な反対に遭った。
His apology did little to soften her implacable hostility toward him. — 彼が謝っても、彼女の彼に対する強い敵意はほとんど和らがなかった。
The editor was relentless in asking for revisions, while the author remained implacably opposed to changing the ending. — 編集者は粘り強く修正を求め続け、著者は結末の変更に断固として反対し続けた。

usage.object: The object is typically an angry or dissatisfied person or group. With or by can introduce what is offered or done to calm them.

en: to make someone less angry or dissatisfied, especially by saying or doing something to address their reaction
ja: （怒っている人・不満を持つ人を）なだめる、怒りや不満を和らげる

nuance.ja: すでに怒っている、反発している、あるいは不満を抱いている相手に、説明・謝罪・譲歩などで働きかける場面に合う。try to placate residents なら、住民の反発を抑えようとすること。何が不満の原因かを解決できたかは文脈次第で、表面的な対応だと批判する文脈にも使われる。
nuance.en: Placate often refers to addressing someone who is already angry or dissatisfied, for example with an explanation, apology, or concession. It can describe a genuine effort to calm tensions or an attempt to quiet objections without addressing their cause.

en: calm down: Broadly describes reducing agitation or excitement. Placate typically involves responding to anger, dissatisfaction, or opposition.
appease: Often suggests pacifying someone by meeting demands or making concessions. It can imply excessive accommodation, especially in politics.
mollify: A close, somewhat formal synonym that can suggest softening someone’s anger or hurt feelings.
implacable: Describes a person or hostile attitude that efforts to placate cannot soften.
ja: calm down：興奮や動揺を広く鎮める。placate は怒りや不満、反発のある相手に働きかける場面で使いやすい。
appease：要求を受け入れたり譲歩したりして相手をなだめる響きが出やすく、政治では譲りすぎという批判を帯びることがある。
mollify：怒りや傷ついた気持ちを和らげる、やや改まった類義語。
implacable：なだめようとしても態度や敵意が和らがない。

note.ja: 人の怒りや不満を和らげる。
note.en: Soften someone’s anger or resentment.

note.ja: 要求に応じるなどして相手をなだめる。
note.en: Pacify someone, often by making concessions.

etymology.ja: ラテン語 placāre「なだめる、鎮める」にさかのぼる。英語では placation から作られたとする説と、ラテン語の過去分詞 placātus に由来するとする説がある。前のカード implacable と同系。
etymology.en: Ultimately from Latin placāre, ‘to soothe or appease.’ English may have formed the verb from placation or taken it from Latin placātus, the past participle. Implacable belongs to the same word family.

usage.agreement: Use singular agreement: Consumer spending has risen. For individual items, use expenses, purchases, or payments, depending on the context.

en: the act or pattern of using money to buy goods or services or pay for activities
the amount of money spent by a person, group, or government
ja: お金を使うこと、出費、支出
（家計・企業・政府などの）支出額、消費額

nuance.ja: 一定の期間や分野で、誰が何にどれだけお金を使うかを述べるときに便利。spending on eating out は外食への出費、consumer spending は消費者支出。cut spending は実際の支出を減らすことを表す。家計などで個々の費用を挙げるなら travel expenses のように expenses がよく合う。
nuance.en: Spending often describes the total, pattern, or trend of money spent by a person or group. Spending on eating out singles out one category, while consumer spending describes what consumers spend collectively. Expenses often names particular costs, as in travel expenses.

en: expenditure: Overlaps with spending and sounds more formal, especially in accounts and reports. Capital expenditure is an established accounting term.
expenses: Costs incurred for particular needs or activities. Travel expenses can include individual fares and hotel charges.
budget: A plan or amount set aside in advance. Spending is the money actually used, or the act of using it.
cost: What a product or activity costs. Spending focuses on what a person or organization pays out.
ja: expenditure：spending と意味が重なり、会計や報告書ではより改まった表現。capital expenditure は「資本的支出」という定着した会計用語。
expenses：特定の活動や用事のためにかかる費用。travel expenses には交通費や宿泊費など個々の費用が含まれる。
budget：事前に立てる資金計画や使える金額。spending は実際にお金を使うことや使った金額を指す。
cost：品物や活動にいくらかかるか。spending は人や組織がいくら使うかに焦点がある。

note.ja: 支出。公的・会計的な文脈でよく使う。
note.en: Money spent, especially in formal or financial contexts.

note.ja: 特定の目的に投じる金額。
note.en: An amount spent for a particular purpose.

etymology.ja: 動詞 spend「お金・時間などを使う」に -ing が付いた形。名詞として単独で使う spending は、ふつう金銭の支出を表す。spending time with family の spending は動詞 spend の -ing 形。
etymology.en: Formed from spend and -ing. The standalone noun usually refers to money. In spending time with family, spending is the -ing form of the verb spend.

en: to use money to buy or pay for something
to pass time in a place, with someone, or doing something

（ある場所や人と、あることをして時間を）過ごす、（時間を）費やす

nuance.ja: spend はお金や時間を使う人・組織を主語にする。spend $40 on groceries では on で使い道を示し、spend two hours reading では -ing 形でその間の行動を示す。spend the weekend with friends のように、単に誰とどう過ごしたかも表せる。
nuance.en: The subject is the person or organization using the money or time. Use on to name what the money goes toward and an -ing form to describe what someone does during a period of time. Spend can simply describe how time passes, as in spend the weekend with friends.

en: pay: Focuses on making a payment. I paid the plumber $80 names the recipient. I spent $80 on repairs describes where the money went.
cost: The thing or service is the subject. The repair cost me $80 corresponds to I spent $80 on the repair.
take: It took me two hours to write the report describes how long the task took. I spent two hours writing the report describes how I used the time.
spending: As a noun, it usually refers to money used. We spend less on takeout describes what we do. Our spending on takeout fell describes the change in our outgoings.
ja: pay：支払いの行為に焦点がある。I paid the plumber $80 は支払先を、I spent $80 on repairs は80ドルの使い道を示す。
cost：品物やサービスが主語になる。The repair cost me $80 は、使った側を主語にした I spent $80 on the repair に対応する。
take：It took me two hours to write the report は報告書を書くのにかかった時間を、I spent two hours writing the report はその2時間を何に使ったかを述べる。
spending：名詞では主に金銭の「支出」。We spend less on takeout は自分たちの行動を、Our spending on takeout fell は支出額の変化を表す。

note.ja: お金・時間・労力などを使う。use は道具を使うときにも使える。
note.en: A broader verb for using resources, tools, or materials.

note.ja: 目的に時間や労力を割く。devote time to doing something の形を取る。
note.en: To give time or effort to a purpose, as in devote time to doing something.

etymology.ja: 中英語 spenden にさかのぼる。古英語には forspendan があり、その -spendan は中世ラテン語 spendere に由来するとされる。spendere はラテン語 expendere「支払う、費やす」または dispendere「分配する、支払う」の短縮形と考えられている。
etymology.en: From Middle English spenden, with an earlier form in Old English forspendan. The verb is traced to Medieval Latin spendere, likely shortened from Latin expendere or possibly dispendere.

grammar.countability: countable in the senses of a question or an issue
patterns: ask someone a question about something

usage.noun: Say ask a question for the everyday act of asking. In the question of whether to appeal, question means an issue to be decided.
usage.verb: Question someone means to ask them questions, often formally or persistently. Question something, or question whether something is true, means to express doubt or examine it critically.

en: (noun) something you ask in order to get information or an answer
(noun) an issue or point to be discussed or decided
(verb) to ask someone questions, often in an official or serious setting
(verb) to doubt or examine the truth, value, or soundness of something
ja: （名詞）質問、問い、設問
（名詞）論点、検討すべき問題
（動詞）人に質問する、事情を聴く、問いただす
（動詞）真偽・妥当性などを疑問視する、吟味する

nuance.ja: ask a question は日常の「質問する」。question a witness では人を目的語に取り、証人に事情を聴いたり尋問したりする。question an assumption では前提の妥当性を吟味する。名詞の the question of whether to appeal は「不服申立てをするかどうかという論点」を表す。out of the question は選択肢としてあり得ないという強い表現。
nuance.en: Ask a question is the everyday expression for requesting an answer. With a person as its object, question often suggests formal or sustained questioning, as in question a witness. With a claim or assumption as its object, it expresses scrutiny or doubt. The question of whether to appeal names an issue to be decided. Out of the question rules an option out.

en: ask: A broad verb used for requests and ordinary questions. I asked her where she was going. I questioned her about where she was going sounds more probing.
issue: A topic, difficulty, or concern to address. Question can frame it as a specific point to resolve: The issue is funding. The question is how to raise the money.
doubt: Expresses uncertainty or disbelief. Question can suggest actively examining the basis for a claim: Several reviewers questioned the study’s assumptions.
interrogate: A stronger verb for intensive, often official questioning. Question has a wider range and can also take a claim or decision as its object.
ja: ask：日常的に尋ねたり頼んだりするときに広く使う。I asked her where she was going は単に行き先を尋ねたことを表し、I questioned her about where she was going は詳しく問いただした響きがある。
issue：対処や議論が必要な問題・話題。The issue is funding. は資金が課題だと示し、The question is how to raise the money. はどう調達するかという具体的な問いを立てる。
doubt：真偽などを疑う気持ちを表す。question は、主張や前提の根拠を積極的に吟味する意味でも使える。
interrogate：集中的に問いただす、尋問する。question はより広く、主張や判断を目的語に取って「疑問視する」とも言える。

note.ja: 問い合わせ、調査。情報を求める行為や調査全体を指すこともある。
note.en: A request for information or a broader investigation.

note.ja: 主張や判断などの正しさに異議を唱える。
note.en: To openly dispute a claim, judgment, or assumption.

etymology.ja: 中英語 questioun は、アングロ・フランス語 questiun や古フランス語 question を経由し、ラテン語 quaestiō「探求、調査、尋問」にさかのぼる。語根の quaerere は「探す、尋ねる」を意味する。
etymology.en: Middle English questioun came through Anglo-French and Old French forms and goes back to Latin quaestiō, meaning inquiry or investigation, from quaerere, meaning to seek or ask.

Without the client’s approval, filing today is out of the question. — 依頼人の承認がなければ、今日出願することは到底できない。

usage.history: A plebeian is a member of the Roman plebs. The adjective in plebeian rights or plebeian families is a historical description.
usage.modern: In modern figurative use the adjective is formal and usually disparaging. It can be ironic or self-mocking when someone applies it to their own tastes.

en: (noun, historical) a member of the plebs, the common people of ancient Rome
(adjective, historical) relating to the Roman plebs
(adjective, formal and often disparaging) associated with ordinary people or regarded as lacking refinement
(noun, formal and often disparaging) a commoner or someone regarded as low in social rank
ja: （名詞・歴史）古代ローマの平民、プレブスの一員
（形容詞・歴史）古代ローマの平民の、プレブスに関する
（形容詞・改まった語、しばしば侮蔑的）庶民の、庶民的な、洗練を欠くとみなされた
（名詞・改まった語、しばしば侮蔑的）庶民、身分が低いとみなされた人

nuance.ja: 古代ローマ史では patrician（貴族・パトリキ）と対をなす身分上の呼称。plebeian には裕福な人もいた。現代の plebeian tastes は、好みを「庶民的で洗練されていない」と見下す響きが出やすい。自分の好みについて使えば、気取った価値観をからかう冗談にもなる。
nuance.en: In Roman history, plebeian identifies a social order alongside its counterpart patrician, and a plebeian could be wealthy. In modern use, describing tastes as plebeian often sounds snobbish. Using it of your own preferences can playfully mock the idea that they need to be refined.

en: patrician: The historical counterpart in ancient Rome. In modern descriptions it can suggest an aristocratic background or manner.
commoner: A broader term for someone outside a noble or privileged rank, especially in a society with formal social ranks.
lowbrow: Informal, often used about entertainment or taste regarded as intellectually unsophisticated. Plebeian adds a social-class undertone.
pleb: A colloquial shortening used as an insult or a joke. Plebeian is the formal word and the usual term in Roman history.
ja: patrician：古代ローマで plebeian と対をなす貴族。現代では貴族的な出自や物腰を表すこともある。
commoner：貴族などの特権的な身分に属さない人を広く表す。身分制度のある社会について使いやすい。
lowbrow：知的な洗練に欠けるとされる娯楽や趣味を指すくだけた語。plebeian には社会階層を意識した響きがある。
pleb：くだけた短縮形。悪口や冗談に使う。古代ローマ史の説明では通常 plebeian を使う。

note.ja: 名詞。身分制度の文脈で「平民、庶民」。
note.en: A person outside the nobility or another privileged rank.

note.ja: 形容詞。趣味や振る舞いが洗練されていないと評価するとき。
note.en: Describes tastes or manners regarded as lacking polish.

etymology.ja: ラテン語 plēbēius「平民に属する」に由来し、そのもとに plēbs（属格 plēbis）「民衆、平民」がある。plebiscite「国民投票・住民投票」も同じ語根を持つ。
etymology.en: From Latin plēbēius, meaning ‘of the common people,’ from plēbs (genitive plēbis), ‘the common people.’ Plebiscite contains the same Latin root.

usage.noun: Use the hyphenated form for the informal noun: She has plenty of get-up-and-go. Common modifiers include real, some, and plenty of.
usage.verbSequence: Use spaces when get up and go are separate verbs joined by and: We got up and went to the station. Both verbs change tense.

en: (informal) energy and enthusiasm that make someone ready to take action
the drive and initiative to get things moving
ja: （口語）物事に取りかかる活力、やる気
自分から動いて物事を進める行動力、意欲

nuance.ja: 元気さに加えて、自分から動き出す勢いを感じさせる口語表現。She’s got real get-up-and-go. は、指示を待たずに動ける人を褒める言い方。I’ve lost my get-up-and-go. のように、そのときの気力や元気が落ちたことにも使える。名詞はハイフンでつなぎ、文字どおり「起き上がって行く」と言うときは get up and go と書く。
nuance.en: This informal noun suggests energy put into action. Saying someone has real get-up-and-go can praise their willingness to get things started. You can also talk about losing your get-up-and-go when you feel temporarily low on energy or motivation. The hyphens mark the noun, while get up and go can be an ordinary sequence of verbs.

en: energy: The broad term for physical or mental capacity to do things. Get-up-and-go suggests readiness to use that energy and get moving.
initiative: The ability to notice what needs doing and act independently. Get-up-and-go also conveys vigor and enthusiasm.
drive: Strong motivation, often sustained and directed toward a goal. Get-up-and-go has a more conversational feel and can describe how energetic you feel today.
enthusiasm: Eagerness or excitement about something. Get-up-and-go emphasizes the energy that gets someone moving.
ja: energy：身体や心のエネルギーを広く指す。get-up-and-go には、その元気を行動に移す勢いがある。
initiative：必要なことに気づき、自分の判断で動く力。get-up-and-go はそこに元気さや意気込みも感じさせる。
drive：目標に向かって持続する強い意欲を指すことが多い。get-up-and-go はより口語的で、その日の気力にも使える。
enthusiasm：何かに対する熱意やわくわくした気持ち。get-up-and-go は、実際に動き出す活力に重点がある。

note.ja: 目標に向かう強い意欲、原動力。
note.en: Strong motivation to pursue a goal.

note.ja: 指示を待たずに自分から動く力。
note.en: The ability to act independently when something needs doing.

etymology.ja: get up「起き上がる」と go「行く、動き出す」を and でつないだ get up and go を、ひとまとまりの名詞にした表現。「腰を上げて動き出す」という動作が、活力や行動力を表すようになった。名詞の用例は20世紀初頭に記録されている。
etymology.en: The noun comes from the sequence get up and go, which evokes rising and setting out. The action became an image for energy and readiness to act. The noun is recorded in the early twentieth century.

ja: Maya has real get-up-and-go. By Friday, she’d already found a venue and signed up three volunteers. — マヤは本当に行動力がある。金曜までにもう会場を見つけて、ボランティアを3人集めていた。

usage.spelling: A common spelling pattern is dirt cheap after a linking verb or as an adverb, and dirt-cheap before a noun: The flights are dirt cheap. We found dirt-cheap flights. Some dictionaries also list dirt-cheap as the headword.
usage.adverb: After buy, get, or sell, it describes the price of the transaction: We bought the table dirt cheap.

en: (adjective, informal) extremely inexpensive
(adverb, informal) at an extremely low price
ja: （形容詞・口語）ものすごく安い、激安の
（副詞・口語）激安で、二束三文で

nuance.ja: 予想や相場に比べて驚くほど安いときの、くだけた強調表現。買い手が掘り出し物を喜ぶ場合にも、売り手が安すぎる値段で手放す場合にも使える。値段に焦点があり、品質については文脈が決める。dirt-cheap flights のように名詞の前ではハイフンでつなぐのが一般的。
nuance.en: A conversational way to emphasize a surprisingly low price. It can express delight at a bargain or highlight how little a seller received. The phrase focuses on price, and the context tells you about quality.

en: cheap: A broad word for a low price that can also imply poor quality. Dirt cheap intensifies the price meaning.
affordable: Within someone’s budget. A price can be affordable even if it is close to the usual price.
a bargain: A good deal for what you get. Dirt cheap emphasizes how little you pay.
for next to nothing: An informal price expression used with verbs such as buy, get, and sell. Dirt cheap also works as a description after be or before a noun.
ja: cheap：安いという広い意味のほか、「安っぽい」の意味もある。dirt cheap は値段の安さを強調する。
affordable：予算内で買える、手が届く。相場並みの価格でも、予算内なら affordable と言える。
a bargain：値段に対して得られるものがお得な買い物。dirt cheap は支払う金額の低さに重点がある。
for next to nothing：買う・売るなどの動詞と合わせる「ほとんどただ同然で」。dirt cheap は be の後や名詞の前でも値段を形容できる。

note.ja: 「土ほど安い」という、同じ比喩を使ったくだけた言い方。
note.en: An informal comparison using the same image.

note.ja: 「非常に安価な」。値段を落ち着いた調子で伝える言い方。
note.en: A neutral way to describe a very low price.

etymology.ja: cheap as dirt「土ほど安い」を縮めた表現。どこにでもある土を、ほとんど値打ちのないものにたとえて、cheap を強めている。
etymology.en: A shortened form of cheap as dirt. The comparison treats ordinary soil as something of very little monetary value to emphasize how low the price is.

patterns: I’d bet dollars to doughnuts (that) + clause
I’ll bet dollars to doughnuts (that) + clause

usage.preposition: The established idiom uses to. Dollars for doughnuts would ordinarily suggest money paid or given for doughnuts.
usage.spelling: Doughnuts and donuts are both used in the idiom.
usage.clause: That can be omitted after bet. The clause can describe a future event, a present situation, or a guess about the past.

en: (informal, chiefly US) used to emphasize that you are very sure something is true or will happen
in I’d bet dollars to doughnuts, a playful way to say you would confidently bet on a prediction or guess
ja: （主に米・口語）きっと〜だ、〜に違いない
I’d bet dollars to doughnuts の形で「賭けてもいいが、きっと〜だ」

nuance.ja: 自分の見立てにかなり自信があるときに、架空の賭けにたとえて言う。相手との会話で、軽い冗談めかした響きを添えられる。未来の予想だけでなく、I’d bet dollars to doughnuts he sent it to the wrong address. のように、過去に起きたことについての推測にも使う。
nuance.en: A colorful, often playful way to show strong confidence in a prediction or inference. The bet is usually figurative. It works for guesses about the past as well as predictions about the future.

en: I bet (that) ...: The everyday, shorter way to express a confident guess. Dollars to doughnuts makes the wager more vivid.
I’d wager (that) ...: A slightly more formal way to make a confident prediction or inference.
I’m certain (that) ...: States certainty directly and suits more neutral or formal contexts.
odds are (that) ...: Says something is likely. Dollars to doughnuts often conveys a stronger degree of personal confidence.
ja: I bet (that) ...：自信のある推測を示す日常的な言い方。dollars to doughnuts を添えると賭けの比喩が際立つ。
I’d wager (that) ...：「賭けてもいい」と言う、やや改まった表現。
I’m certain (that) ...：「確信している」と直接伝える。中立的・改まった文脈にも合う。
odds are (that) ...：「たぶん〜だ」「〜の可能性が高い」。dollars to doughnuts は話し手自身の強い確信を感じさせやすい。

note.ja: 直前に述べたことに「賭けてもいい」と強い自信を示す。
note.en: Shows strong confidence in what has just been said.

note.ja: 「かなり確かだと思う」という日常的な言い方。
note.en: An everyday expression of fairly strong confidence.

etymology.ja: 19世紀の米国に用例がある賭けの比喩。相手が当時安価だったドーナツを賭けるのに対して、自分はそれより価値の高いドルを賭けてもいい、という発想で、勝つ見込みへの自信を表す。
etymology.en: An American betting expression recorded in the nineteenth century. It imagines staking dollars against doughnuts, then worth much less, because you are confident you will win.

patterns: during / through the dog days of summer
in the middle of the dog days of summer
the dog days of summer are here
the dog days of + period or activity

usage.summer: The phrase normally takes the definite article and plural agreement: The dog days of summer are here.
usage.figurative: Dog days can also describe a sluggish or stagnant stretch, as in the dog days of the campaign.

en: the hottest, often most oppressive stretch of summer
(short form dog days, figurative) a stretch when little happens or progress stalls
ja: 夏の最も暑い時期、うだるような暑さが続く真夏の日々
（短い形 dog days の比喩用法）停滞期、物事が進まない時期

nuance.ja: 一日だけの暑さより、暑さが続く真夏のひと時期を指す。暑さで人通りや仕事のペースが落ちるような情景にもよく合うが、夏の暑い盛りを述べるだけでも使える。the dog days of the campaign のように、季節を問わず活動に勢いがなくなる時期も表せる。
nuance.en: The phrase evokes a stretch of oppressive summer heat, sometimes with a sense that life has slowed down. It can simply set the scene in high summer. In phrases such as the dog days of the campaign, it describes a lull at any time of year.

en: heat wave: A spell of unusually hot weather relative to local conditions. The dog days of summer names a seasonal stretch when intense heat is expected.
the height of summer: The peak of the season, which can evoke holidays or long days as well as heat. Dog days puts the heat in the foreground.
a lull: A temporary quiet spell in any activity. The figurative dog days can suggest a longer, sluggish phase.
ja: heat wave：その土地の平年の気候に比べて異常な暑さが続く「熱波」。dog days of summer は暑さが例年訪れる真夏の時期を指す。
the height of summer：夏の盛り。暑さに加え、休暇や日が長いことなども連想させる。dog days は特に暑さに焦点がある。
a lull：活動の一時的な小休止。比喩の dog days は、勢いのない状態がしばらく続く感じを出せる。

note.ja: 夏の最も暑い時期を直接表す。
note.en: A plain description of the hottest stretch of the season.

note.ja: 比喩用法に近く、仕事や活動の動きが鈍い時期。
note.en: A stretch of reduced activity, close to the figurative sense.

etymology.ja: dog days はラテン語 diēs canīculārēs の訳に由来する。canīcula は文字どおりには「小犬」で、ここではおおいぬ座のシリウス（Dog Star）を指す。古代の地中海世界では、この星が日の出前の空に再び見える頃と夏の酷暑が結びつけられていた。
etymology.en: Dog days is a translation of Latin diēs canīculārēs. Canīcula literally means ‘little dog’ and here names Sirius, the Dog Star in Canis Major. In the ancient Mediterranean world, the star’s reappearance shortly before sunrise was associated with the hottest part of summer.

patterns: grab / get a cup of joe
pour someone a cup of joe
I could use a cup of joe

usage.article: Use a determiner with the singular cup: a cup of joe, my cup of joe, or another cup of joe.
usage.spelling: Lowercase joe is usual when it means coffee. Cup o’ joe is a playful spelling that reflects casual speech.

en: (informal, chiefly US) a cup of coffee
ja: （主に米・口語）コーヒー一杯

nuance.ja: コーヒーを親しみのある調子で呼ぶ米国の口語表現。朝の一杯や仕事の合間のコーヒーなど、日常の場面によく合う。ダイナーで出る普通のコーヒーを連想させることもあるが、豆や淹れ方、ミルクの有無はこの表現だけでは決まらない。I could use a cup of joe. は「コーヒーでも一杯飲みたいな」という気分を表す。
nuance.en: A casual American way to refer to a cup of coffee, with a friendly or slightly playful tone. It often evokes an everyday coffee break or morning routine. The phrase leaves the brewing method and additions unspecified. I could use a cup of joe sounds like a personal wish for a coffee break or a pick-me-up.

en: a cup of coffee: A neutral expression for the same drink in conversation, orders, and writing. Cup of joe adds a casual American tone.
a shot of espresso: Specifies a small serving of espresso. A cup of joe can evoke ordinary brewed coffee in a diner setting.
a cuppa: In British English this informal noun typically means a cup of tea. Cup of joe specifically means coffee.
ja: a cup of coffee：会話、注文、文章で使える中立的な言い方。cup of joe には米国のくだけた響きがある。
a shot of espresso：少量のエスプレッソ一杯。cup of joe はダイナーなどでは普通のドリップコーヒーを連想させることがある。
a cuppa：イギリス英語の口語で、ふつう紅茶一杯。cup of joe はコーヒーを指す。

note.ja: 同じ飲み物を指す、場面を選ばない表現。
note.en: The neutral equivalent.

usage.spelling: Curveball is the main dictionary spelling. Curve ball and, especially in American English, curve are also used.
usage.figurative: In throw someone a curveball, the subject can be a person or an event. The phrase often suggests that the surprise forces someone to adjust.

en: (baseball) a pitch that curves on its way to the batter
(figurative, informal) an unexpected question, event, or change that is difficult to deal with
ja: （野球）カーブ、打者に向かう途中で軌道が曲がる球
（比喩・口語）不意を突く質問、対応を迫られる予想外の出来事や変更

nuance.ja: 比喩では、予想外のことに出くわして、とっさに考え直したり予定を変えたりする感じがある。The interviewer threw me a curveball. なら「面接官に予想外の質問をされた」。The power outage threw us a curveball. のように、停電など人の意図と無関係の出来事も主語にできる。
nuance.en: A figurative curveball catches someone off guard and often makes them think on their feet or change plans. An interviewer can throw you a curveball with an unusual question, and a power outage can throw you one without anyone intending to surprise you.

en: surprise: The broad term for something unexpected, welcome or unwelcome. A curveball often calls for a response or adjustment.
setback: A difficulty that delays or reverses progress. A curveball emphasizes being caught off guard and can sometimes be handled on the spot.
trick question: A question designed to mislead or expose a mistake. A curveball question can simply be outside what you prepared for.
breaking ball: In baseball, a broader category that includes the curveball and other pitches such as the slider.
ja: surprise：うれしいことも困ることも含めた「驚き、予想外のこと」。curveball には、そこから対応を迫られる感じがある。
setback：進捗を遅らせたり後退させたりする障害。curveball は不意を突かれる点に重点があり、その場で対応できることもある。
trick question：相手を引っかける意図のある質問。curveball は、単に準備していなかった質問にも使える。
breaking ball：野球ではカーブやスライダーなどを含む、より広い球種の呼び方。

note.ja: 野球と比喩の両方で使える短い形。throw someone a curve とも言う。
note.en: A shorter form used both in baseball and in throw someone a curve.

note.ja: 状況への対応を難しくする予想外の問題。
note.en: An unforeseen problem that makes a situation harder to handle.

etymology.ja: curve「曲がる、曲線」と ball「球」を組み合わせた野球用語。打者が予想した軌道から外れる球のイメージから、人の不意を突く質問や出来事にも使われるようになった。
etymology.en: From curve and ball, originally a baseball term. The pitch can catch a batter expecting a different trajectory off guard. That image gave rise to the figurative sense of a surprise that is hard to handle.

patterns: if + clause, someone’s goose is cooked

usage.cause: The subject can be a person’s action or an event: The last-minute withdrawal cooked our goose.
usage.result: My goose is cooked means ‘I’m done for.’ Change the possessive to match the person or group affected: his goose, our goose, the team's goose.

en: (informal) to ruin someone’s plans or chances of success, often decisively
(someone’s goose is cooked) someone is doomed to fail or in trouble they are unlikely to get out of
ja: （口語）人の計画を台無しにする、成功の望みをつぶす
（someone’s goose is cooked の形で）もうおしまいだ、もはや助かりそうにない

nuance.ja: 何かが決定打となり、挽回が難しくなった場面で使う。自分の失敗が原因なら cook one’s own goose（自分で自分の首を絞める）とも言う。My goose is cooked. は「もうおしまいだ」と結果に焦点を当てた言い方で、重大な失敗にも、日常の失敗を大げさに語る冗談にも使える。
nuance.en: The idiom often points to a decisive event or mistake that leaves little chance of recovery. Cook one’s own goose makes the setback self-inflicted. My goose is cooked focuses on the likely outcome and can sound wry or humorously dramatic.

en: spoil someone’s plans: A broad expression that can cover a minor disruption. Cook someone’s goose often suggests a decisive blow.
be done for: A close match for someone’s goose is cooked. It describes the person’s predicament.
shoot oneself in the foot: To undermine oneself through one’s own actions. Cook one’s own goose often suggests graver consequences.
kill the goose that lays the golden eggs: To destroy a continuing source of profit or benefit, often for a short-term gain.
ja: spoil someone’s plans：人の計画を台無しにする。小さな予定の狂いにも使える一方、cook someone’s goose は決定的な痛手を表すことが多い。
be done for：「もうおしまいだ」。someone’s goose is cooked と同様に、窮地に陥った人の状態を述べる。
shoot oneself in the foot：自分の行動で自分に不利益を招く。cook one’s own goose は、挽回が難しいほどの結果を示すことが多い。
kill the goose that lays the golden eggs：目先の利益などのために、継続的な利益を生む源をつぶす。

note.ja: 人の成功の望みをつぶす。比喩を使わず直接伝える表現。
note.en: A direct way to say that someone’s prospects of success have been ruined.

note.ja: 「もうおしまいだ」という結果を表す口語。
note.en: An informal way to describe an apparently hopeless position.

etymology.ja: 直訳は「人のガチョウを料理する」。cook his goose などの形は1830年代の英国の文献に見られるが、なぜこの比喩が生まれたかは分かっていない。語源として語られる逸話には確かな裏づけがない。
etymology.en: Literally ‘to cook someone’s goose.’ Forms such as cook his goose are recorded in British writing in the 1830s. How the figurative sense arose remains uncertain, and the colorful stories attached to it lack firm evidence.

patterns: coin a term to describe + noun

usage.creation: Use coin as a verb with a word, term, or phrase as its object: They coined a term for it. Use the phrase when naming the wording or referring to an expression already identified.
usage.parenthetical: Set off the humorous aside to coin a phrase with commas when it interrupts a sentence.
usage.spelling: The expression uses phrase ‘a group of words.’ Phase means a stage or period, as in the next phase of a project.

en: to invent a new expression
(to coin a phrase, humorous aside) used to introduce or draw attention to a familiar expression or cliché
ja: 新しい言い回しを作る、表現を生み出す
（to coin a phrase の形で、冗談めかして）お決まりの言い方を借りれば、月並みな言い方だけれど

nuance.ja: She coined a phrase for it. なら、彼女がそれを表す新しい言い回しを作った、という意味。文中に挟む to coin a phrase は、よく知られた言い回しを、いま自分で作ったかのように持ち出す冗談になる。古い言い回しを使うことへの軽い照れや、聞き手への目配せが感じられる。
nuance.en: She coined a phrase for it credits her with inventing the wording. The parenthetical to coin a phrase often playfully treats a familiar expression as if it had just been invented, with a wink to the listener.

en: coin a term: Invent a name or label for a concept. Coin a phrase can describe the creation of a longer expression.
come up with a phrase: An everyday way to say you thought of some wording. Coin suggests giving the language or a group a new expression.
to use a cliché: Openly signals that a familiar expression follows. To coin a phrase can do the same with a touch of irony.
popularize a phrase: Make an expression widely known. The person who popularizes it may be different from the person who coined it.
ja: coin a term：ある概念を指す新しい用語や呼び名を作る。coin a phrase は複数語からなる言い回しを作るときにも使う。
come up with a phrase：言い回しを思いつくという日常的な表現。coin は、それまでなかった言い回しを生み出すことを示す。
to use a cliché：「決まり文句を使えば」と明示する。to coin a phrase はそこに軽い皮肉を添えられる。
popularize a phrase：言い回しを広める。作った人と広めた人は別の場合がある。

note.ja: 言い回しを新しく作る、という意味を直接表す。
note.en: A direct equivalent for creating new wording.

note.ja: 「ことわざにもあるように」。決まり文句を持ち出す場面で使う。
note.en: Introduces a familiar saying and can be used without irony.

etymology.ja: 動詞 coin の「硬貨を鋳造する」という意味から、新しい語や言い回しを作ることを表す比喩が生まれた。よく知られた表現を新作のように紹介する to coin a phrase の用法は、この比喩を逆手に取った冗談。
etymology.en: The verb coin originally refers to minting money. It was extended figuratively to the creation of words and expressions. The humorous aside plays on that sense by presenting familiar wording as though it were newly minted.

patterns: It was close but no cigar for + person or group

usage.response: Use it as a standalone response to a nearly correct guess or as a comment on an attempt that nearly succeeded.
usage.pronunciation: Close means near and ends in /s/, as in a close call. Cigar is stressed on the second syllable.

en: (informal) used when an answer is nearly correct or an attempt falls just short of success
ja: （口語）惜しいけど正解じゃない、あと一歩だったが届かなかった

nuance.ja: 正解や目標にかなり近かったことを認めつつ、届かなかったことを冗談めかして言う。クイズの答えに返すときも、自分たちがあと一歩で勝てなかったと振り返るときも使える。相手の失敗に対して使うと、口調によってはからかっているように聞こえる。
nuance.en: It acknowledges how close someone came while treating the miss with a touch of humor. It works as a reply to a guess or as a wry summary of your own near miss. Said about someone else’s failure, it can sound teasing.

en: almost: Simply indicates that someone nearly reached a goal or gave the right answer. Close but no cigar adds a playful verdict.
nice try: Can praise the effort or dismiss a trick, and can be said even if the attempt was far off.
a near miss: A noun phrase that can describe a narrow failure or a narrowly avoided accident.
a close call: Often expresses relief that something bad almost happened but was avoided. Close but no cigar usually concerns a desired result that was missed.
ja: almost：「もう少しで」「ほぼ」。単独の返事なら「惜しい」。close but no cigar には冗談めかした響きがある。
nice try：「よくやった」や、冗談で「そうはいかないよ」。試みが正解や成功から遠くても使える。
a near miss：「惜しくも届かなかったこと」や「間一髪で事故を免れたこと」を表す名詞句。
a close call：「危ないところだった」。望ましくない結果を間一髪で免れたときによく使う。

note.ja: 答えや推測に「もう少し」「ちょっと違う」と返す短い言い方。
note.en: A brief reply to a guess or answer that is not quite right.

note.ja: 目標まであとわずかのところで届かない。
note.en: To miss a goal by a small margin.

etymology.ja: 昔の縁日や遊園地のゲームで、勝者に葉巻（cigar）を景品として渡した習慣に由来するとされる。「惜しいが、景品の葉巻はなし」という発想から、クイズや競技などの惜しい失敗にも使われるようになった。
etymology.en: The expression is generally traced to fairground games that awarded cigars as prizes. Coming close still meant going away without a cigar, an image that later applied to near misses of all kinds.

patterns: start / begin with a clean slate

usage.article: The noun phrase normally takes a: Let’s start with a clean slate.
usage.related: Wipe the slate clean uses the and focuses on clearing the previous record or setting past grievances aside. Start with a clean slate focuses on the situation you start from.

en: a chance or situation in which you can start again without past events, mistakes, or obligations weighing on the new start
ja: 過去の経緯・失敗・しがらみを白紙にして再出発できる状態や機会

nuance.ja: 過去の失敗や対立、以前の取り決めをいったん脇に置き、改めて始められることに焦点がある。交渉や人間関係でよく合う。wipe the slate clean は過去の記録やわだかまりを消す行為、start with a clean slate はまっさらな状態から始めることを表す。
nuance.en: The image is of being free to begin again without carrying past mistakes, disagreements, or arrangements into the next attempt. Wipe the slate clean emphasizes clearing what came before. Start with a clean slate emphasizes the position from which you begin again.

en: a fresh start: A new beginning, often welcome. A clean slate adds the idea that the past has been put aside.
a blank slate: Also describes something with no entries, content, or established assumptions yet. A clean slate often emphasizes the freedom to begin again after an earlier experience.
start from scratch: Start from the very beginning, often rebuilding without reusing previous work. Start with a clean slate highlights leaving prior baggage behind.
ja: a fresh start：心機一転、新たな出発。a clean slate には、過去の経緯をいったん白紙にするイメージがある。
a blank slate：まだ何も書かれていない状態や、前提が置かれていない状態も表す。a clean slate は、以前の経緯を脇に置いてやり直せることを強調しやすい。
start from scratch：一から始める。既存の成果を使い回さずに作り直す場合にも使う。start with a clean slate は、過去のしがらみを持ち込まずに始める点に重点がある。

note.ja: 新しいスタート、再出発。
note.en: A new beginning.

note.ja: やり直す機会を直接表す。
note.en: An opportunity to begin again.

etymology.ja: slate はここではチョークなどで書く石板。書いてあったものを拭き取って、また書き始める様子が比喩になった。酒場で客の掛け勘定を石板に記し、精算すると消した習慣に結びつける説明がある。
etymology.en: A slate was a writing tablet whose marks could be wiped away. The expression draws on the image of clearing it for reuse. One account connects the image with tavern customers’ running tabs, written on slates and erased when settled.

patterns: I don’t want to steal your thunder

usage.possessive: Use a possessive such as my, her, our, or the team’s. Thunder stays singular in the idiom.
usage.intent: The attention can shift deliberately or by accident. An event can also be the subject.

en: to take attention or credit away from someone who was about to receive it
to lessen the impact of someone’s announcement or idea by revealing it first or presenting it as your own
ja: 人の見せ場を奪う、人に向くはずだった注目や称賛をさらう
人の発表を先取りしたり、アイデアを自分のものとして披露したりして、その人の見せ場を奪う

nuance.ja: 誰かが注目されるはずだった場面で、別の人や出来事に注目が移ることを表す。先に知らせを発表する場合にも、別のニュースが偶然重なって話題をさらう場合にも使える。I don’t want to steal your thunder. は、相手に自分の口から発表してもらいたいときの気遣いとして使える。
nuance.en: The idiom suggests that someone loses a moment of attention or recognition they were about to have. It may involve a deliberate effort to get in first or a coincidental event that draws attention away. I don’t want to steal your thunder can be a tactful way to leave someone else’s news for them to share.

en: steal the show: Attract the most attention or praise at an event. Steal someone’s thunder identifies the person whose moment is diminished.
steal the spotlight: Draw attention to yourself or away from someone else. Steal someone’s thunder often involves a specific announcement or achievement losing its impact.
upstage someone: Overshadow someone in a performance or social situation. Steal someone’s thunder often suggests getting in before a planned reveal.

take credit for someone’s work: Claim recognition for work another person did. Steal someone’s thunder also covers situations where nobody claims authorship, such as announcing someone’s news before they can.
ja: steal the show：その場でいちばん注目や称賛を集める。steal someone’s thunder は誰の見せ場が奪われたかを示す。
steal the spotlight：自分に注目を集めたり、注目を他の人からそらしたりする。steal someone’s thunder は特定の発表や成果のインパクトが薄れる場面によく合う。
upstage someone：舞台や人前で相手をかすませる。steal someone’s thunder は、予定されていた発表の先を越す場合にもよく使う。
take credit for someone’s work：他人の仕事を自分の手柄にする。steal someone’s thunder は、本人に先んじてニュースを明かす場合にも使える。

note.ja: 人より目立ってその人をかすませる。
note.en: To draw attention away from someone by overshadowing them.

note.ja: 本人より先に発表する、発表を先取りする。
note.en: To get ahead of an announcement someone was planning to make.

etymology.ja: 18世紀初頭の英国の劇作家ジョン・デニスにまつわる逸話に由来するとされる。自作の劇のために雷鳴の効果音を工夫したところ、打ち切り後に同じ劇場の別の演目でその効果音が使われ、雷鳴を取られたと抗議したという。
etymology.en: Traditionally traced to a story about the English playwright John Dennis in the early eighteenth century. After his play closed, he reportedly heard a thunder effect he had devised for it in another production and protested that his thunder had been taken.

usage.verb: Have is the usual verb for saying the advantage is available. Keep suggests deliberately holding it in reserve.

en: a secret advantage, resource, or tactic kept in reserve to use when it can make a difference

nuance.ja: 交渉や競争で、相手がまだ知らない有利な材料を、効果の大きい場面まで温存しているときに使う。別の買い手からの提案や、まだ発表していない機能などにも使え、ずるをしているという意味は通常伴わない。still have an ace up one’s sleeve なら、手詰まりに見えてもまだ打てる手がある、という響き。
nuance.en: The phrase suggests that someone has kept a potentially decisive advantage secret until it can help. It can refer to an alternative offer or an unreleased feature, without implying dishonesty. Still have an ace up one’s sleeve suggests there is another move available even when the situation looks difficult.

en: a card up one’s sleeve: A close alternative. Ace emphasizes how strong or decisive the hidden option may be.
an ace in the hole: A close alternative, especially in American English. Its image is a concealed card in poker.
a backup plan: An option to use if the main plan fails. It can be known to everyone. An ace up one’s sleeve is typically hidden and can be used to gain an advantage.
play one’s trump card: Use a decisive advantage at the right moment. Have an ace up one’s sleeve describes having that advantage in reserve.
ja: a card up one’s sleeve：よく似た表現。ace を使うと、その手が強力で決め手になりうることを強調できる。
an ace in the hole：特に米国で使われる近い表現。ポーカーで他のプレイヤーに見えない札が比喩のもと。

play one’s trump card：切り札を実際に切ること。have an ace up one’s sleeve は、切り札を手元に温存している状態を表す。

note.ja: 他人が知らない有利な手段や強み。「秘密兵器」。

note.ja: まだ知られていない有利な材料を直接表す。

etymology.ja: カードゲームで強い札であるエースを袖に隠し、必要なときに取り出すイメージに由来する。そこから、勝負どころまで秘密にしておく有利な手を表すようになった。
etymology.en: The image comes from card play, where a cheat might conceal a valuable ace up a sleeve to use later. The idiom extends that image to any hidden advantage kept in reserve.

patterns: run out of gas on the way to + place

usage.subject: A driver or vehicle can be the subject in the literal sense. A person, team, or effort can be the subject in the figurative sense.
usage.aspect: Run out of gas describes reaching the point of depletion. Be running out of gas describes energy or fuel dwindling. Be out of gas describes the resulting state.
usage.regional: Gas is short for gasoline in North American English. In British English, run out of petrol is usual when talking about a car’s fuel.

en: to use up the gasoline in a vehicle’s tank
(informal, chiefly North American) to lose the energy or enthusiasm needed to keep doing something
(figurative) for an effort or process to lose momentum or the means to continue
ja: （車などの）ガソリンが切れる、ガス欠になる
（主に北米・口語）体力や気力が尽きて続けられなくなる

nuance.ja: 燃料が尽きて車が走れなくなるイメージ。比喩では、試合終盤に選手の体力が尽きる場合にも、進んでいた交渉が勢いを失う場合にも使える。We’re running out of gas. は「そろそろ限界だ」、We’re out of gas. は「もう余力がない」という状態を表す。
nuance.en: The image is of a vehicle losing the fuel it needs to keep moving. Figuratively, an athlete may run out of energy late in a game, or a promising effort may lose momentum. We’re running out of gas suggests reserves are dwindling. We’re out of gas describes the state after they are gone.

en: run out of steam: Close in the figurative sense, especially when an activity loses momentum or people lose interest in it.
run on empty: Keep going on very little fuel or energy. Run out of gas marks the point at which the supply is exhausted.
hit the wall: Suddenly struggle to go on, especially in endurance sports. Run out of gas can also describe a gradual loss of momentum.
break down: Stop working because of a fault. A vehicle that runs out of gas has used up its fuel.
ja: run out of steam：比喩用法が近い。活動が勢いを失ったり、続ける意欲が薄れたりする場面にも合う。
run on empty：残りわずかな燃料や気力で何とか動き続ける。run out of gas はそれが尽きる時点に焦点がある。
hit the wall：特に持久系スポーツで、急に体が動かなくなるほどの限界にぶつかる。run out of gas は徐々に勢いが落ちていく場面にも合う。
break down：故障して動かなくなる。車について run out of gas と言えば、燃料を使い切ったことを指す。

note.ja: 活動などが勢いを失うことを直接表す。
note.en: A direct way to say that an effort is no longer moving forward as strongly.

note.ja: 人の体力や気力が尽きることを直接表す。
note.en: A direct way to say that someone has used up their energy.

etymology.ja: run out of「〜を使い切る」と、gasoline「ガソリン」の短縮形 gas から成る。タンクが空になると車が進めなくなることから、人の体力や活動の勢いが尽きることにも使われる。
etymology.en: The phrase combines run out of, meaning to use up a supply, with gas, short for gasoline. The image of an empty fuel tank extends to exhausted people and efforts that can no longer keep going.

forms.full: throw spaghetti at the wall and see what sticks

patterns: throw spaghetti at the wall and see what sticks

usage.full: And see what sticks spells out the idea of waiting to find out which attempts work. In a past narrative the full form can become threw spaghetti at the wall and saw what stuck.
usage.spelling: In the idiom, use uncountable spaghetti and the definite article in the wall.

en: (informal) to try or suggest many things in the hope that some will work or catch on, often with little advance planning
ja: （口語）とにかくいろいろ試したり案を出したりして、どれがうまくいくか、どれが受けるかを見る

nuance.ja: 何が当たるかまだ分からない段階で、案や試みの数を出して反応を見るというイメージ。ブレインストーミングで気軽に案を出す場面にも、方針がないまま手当たり次第に動いていると批判する場面にも使える。and see what sticks を添えると、どれが残るか見極めるところまで表せる。
nuance.en: The image is of putting several possibilities out there and finding out which, if any, work. It can sound playful when brainstorming or critical when someone seems to be trying things at random. And see what sticks makes the idea of observing the results explicit.

en: brainstorm: Generate ideas, often as a deliberate group exercise. Throw spaghetti at the wall can also refer to trying ideas out and often suggests a less structured approach.
trial and error: Learn by trying and adjusting based on results. It can be systematic, while this idiom emphasizes the number and uncertainty of the attempts.
take a shot in the dark: Make a single guess or attempt with little information. Throw spaghetti at the wall typically suggests several attempts.
throw ideas at the wall: A close variant that names ideas directly and is especially natural during brainstorming.
ja: brainstorm：アイデアを出し合う。意図的に設けた会議にも使う。throw spaghetti at the wall は案を実際に試す場面にも使え、手探り感が出やすい。
trial and error：試して結果を見ながら修正する試行錯誤。計画的にも行える。ここでの慣用句は、数を試して何が当たるか分からない感じを出す。
take a shot in the dark：手がかりが乏しい中で一つの推測や試みをする。throw spaghetti at the wall は複数の試みを指すことが多い。
throw ideas at the wall：近い表現で、試すものがアイデアだと明示する。案出しの場面で使いやすい。

etymology.en: The image evokes tossing cooked spaghetti at a wall to see what adheres. Figuratively, what sticks is the idea that catches on or the attempt that succeeds.

patterns: be (just) putting lipstick on a pig
amount to putting lipstick on a pig

usage.short: The shorter form lipstick on a pig can describe the change itself: The rebrand is just lipstick on a pig.
usage.articles: Lipstick has no article here. Use a before pig. Put has the same form in the present base form, simple past, and past participle.

en: (informal, disapproving) to make cosmetic changes to something in an attempt to make it look better while leaving its underlying problems in place
ja: （口語・批判的）根本的な問題を残したまま、見た目だけ取り繕う、うわべだけをよく見せる

nuance.ja: デザインや名前、宣伝の仕方を変えても、製品や制度などの肝心な欠点が残っていると批判するときに使う。欠点を隠そうとした場合にも、改善するつもりだった変更が表面的だと評価する場合にも使える。比喩が辛辣なので、相手の提案に直接使うと強い批判に聞こえる。
nuance.en: This is a pointed criticism of a redesign, rebrand, or other change that leaves the main problem in place. The person making the change might be trying to hide a flaw or might sincerely think the change is an improvement. Used about someone’s proposal, it can sound blunt.

en: paper over the cracks: Cover up weaknesses or disagreements to keep them out of sight. Put lipstick on a pig highlights making something look more appealing while its flaws remain.
a cosmetic change: A change to appearance or presentation. This can be a neutral description. Lipstick on a pig expresses a negative judgment.
sugarcoat: Make bad news or criticism sound less unpleasant, usually through wording. Lipstick on a pig often describes superficial changes to a product, plan, or system.
you can’t make a silk purse out of a sow’s ear: Says that poor raw material is unlikely to produce something fine. Put lipstick on a pig focuses on the cosmetic improvement actually being made.
ja: paper over the cracks：弱点や対立を覆い隠す。put lipstick on a pig は、欠点が残るものを魅力的に見せようとする表面的な変更を指す。
a cosmetic change：外観や見せ方の変更。中立的にも使えるが、lipstick on a pig には批判が込められている。
sugarcoat：悪い知らせや批判を、主に言葉を選んで耳当たりよく伝える。lipstick on a pig は製品・計画・制度などのうわべだけを変える場面によく合う。
you can’t make a silk purse out of a sow’s ear：質の悪い素材から立派なものは作れない、ということわざ。put lipstick on a pig は実際に行う表面的な変更に焦点がある。

note.ja: 表面的な変更を加える。比喩を使わない言い方。
note.en: A plain description of a change that affects only the surface.

note.ja: 見栄えよく整える。文脈によって、実態以上によく見せるという意味にもなる。
note.en: To make something look or sound more appealing, sometimes more appealing than it deserves.

etymology.en: The image is preserved in a modern saying about putting lipstick on a pig and still having a pig. Older English proverbs use similar images of dressing up a pig to illustrate the limits of changing appearances.

patterns: start eating your own dog food

usage.possessive: Match the possessive to the subject: We eat our own dog food. The company eats its own dog food.
usage.spelling: Dog food is normally two words in the idiom, though dogfood also occurs in tech writing. The related term dogfooding is one word.

en: (informal, especially in tech) to use the products or services you make or sell in your own work, often to spot problems users might encounter
ja: （口語・特にIT業界）自社が作ったり販売したりする製品・サービスを自分たちの業務でも使う。利用者が遭遇する問題を見つける目的で行うことも多い。

nuance.ja: 開発チームが、自社アプリを普段の作業に組み込んで使うような場面に合う。公開前に不具合を見つけるためにも、公開後に使い勝手を確かめるためにも使える。「顧客に使ってもらうものなら、まず自分たちも使おう」という含みがある。dogfooding はこの取り組み自体を指す。
nuance.en: The phrase is common in tech when a team uses its own product for real work. This can reveal friction before launch or guide improvements after release. It also carries the idea that a company should be willing to use what it asks customers to use. Dogfooding names the practice.

en: internal testing: Any testing done inside an organization, including scripted tests. Dogfooding often puts the product into regular workflows.
beta testing: Testing a prerelease version with selected users, who may be external. Dogfooding uses the organization’s own people or operations and can continue after launch.
practice what you preach: Live by the advice or principles you promote. Eat your own dog food is more specific to using what you make or sell.
ja: internal testing：社内テスト全般。手順書どおりのテストも含む。dogfooding は製品を普段の業務に組み込んで使うことが多い。
beta testing：公開前の版を選ばれた利用者に試してもらうこと。社外ユーザーも参加できる。dogfooding の主体は自社側で、公開後も続けられる。
practice what you preach：人に勧めることを自分でも実践する。eat your own dog food は、自社の製品やサービスを使う場面に特化した言い方。

note.ja: 自社製品を社内で使う、という中立的な言い方。
note.en: A neutral way to describe using your own product inside the organization.

note.ja: 自社製品を自分たちで使う取り組みを指すIT業界の用語。
note.en: The tech term for the practice itself.

etymology.ja: 「自分たちのドッグフードを食べる」という比喩で、人に売るものを自分たちでも使うという発想を表す。IT業界で広まった経緯として、1988年にマイクロソフト社内で自社製品の利用を促すメールにこの表現が使われた逸話がよく紹介される。表現そのものの起源には諸説ある。

en: (informal business jargon) to take on a task with such a broad scope that it becomes impractical or impossible

nuance.ja: 会議やプロジェクトで、調査や作業の範囲が目的や期限に対して広すぎるときに使う。Let’s not boil the ocean. は「最初から全部やろうとせず、必要なところに絞ろう」という提案。ひとつの小さな疑問に答えるのに、膨大な作業をしようとする場合にも当てはまる。
nuance.en: Common in project discussions when the proposed scope is too broad for the goal, resources, or time available. Let’s not boil the ocean often introduces a narrower first step. It can also criticize a great deal of work aimed at answering a relatively small question.

en: bite off more than you can chew: Take on more than you can handle. Boil the ocean often criticizes the scope of a particular task or approach.
overcomplicate: Make something more complicated than necessary. Boil the ocean emphasizes the scale or effort involved.
reinvent the wheel: Waste effort recreating something that already exists. Boil the ocean concerns excessive scope, whether or not a solution already exists.
ja: bite off more than you can chew：自分の手に余る仕事を引き受ける。boil the ocean は個々の作業や方法の範囲が広すぎると指摘するときに使いやすい。

etymology.en: Literally, to bring the ocean to a boil. The image of an impossibly large undertaking became a metaphor for excessive scope or effort. The original coiner is uncertain.

patterns: keep kicking the can down the road

usage.fixed: The idiom normally keeps both definite articles: the can and the road. The can stands for the matter being put off.
usage.cause: Use by + -ing to say how the decision or action is being put off.

en: (informal, originally US) to put off dealing with a problem or making a difficult decision, leaving it to be dealt with later
ja: （口語・米国発）問題への対処や難しい決断を先送りにする、当面の対応でしのいで解決を後回しにする

nuance.ja: 今向き合うべき問題を、決定や対策なしに先へ送るという批判的な響きが出やすい。政治や仕事では、暫定措置や期限延長を繰り返す場面によく合う。自分が出費や面倒な判断を後回しにしていることを、冗談めかして認めるときにも使える。
nuance.en: It often criticizes delaying a decision that should be made now. In politics or business, it fits repeated extensions or temporary fixes that leave the underlying issue for later. Speakers can also use it wryly about their own reluctance to deal with something.

en: postpone: Move a decision or event to a later time. It can describe a sensible scheduling change. Kick the can down the road often implies avoidance.
buy time: Gain time to prepare or find a solution. A temporary measure that buys time may be useful. Calling it kicking the can down the road suggests the underlying issue is still being ducked.
procrastinate: Put off something you need to do, often as a personal habit. Kick the can down the road is especially useful for decisions put off by teams or institutions.
kick something into the long grass: A similar British idiom for putting an issue aside, sometimes indefinitely.
ja: postpone：予定や決定を後日に延期する。合理的な日程変更にも使える。kick the can down the road には問題への対処を避けている響きが出やすい。
buy time：準備や解決策を探すための時間を稼ぐ。同じ暫定措置でも、kick the can down the road と言うと問題を先送りにしているという評価になる。
procrastinate：やるべきことを後回しにする。個人の先延ばし癖にもよく使う。kick the can down the road は組織の意思決定が先延ばしになる場面にも合う。
kick something into the long grass：問題を棚上げする、場合によっては無期限に先送りする、という英国の類似表現。

etymology.en: The literal image is of kicking a can farther along a road. The can stays in the road, just as an unresolved problem is pushed into the future.

patterns: treat something as a sacred cow

usage.register: The figurative sense is usually critical or ironic and occurs in conversations, business discussions, and commentary.
usage.plural: No sacred cows suggests that any policy, practice, or assumption can be reconsidered.

en: (figurative, usually disapproving) an idea, practice, institution, or person treated as beyond criticism or challenge
ja: （比喩・ふつう批判的）批判や見直しが許されないもの、疑問を差し挟めないとされる考え方・慣行・制度・人物

nuance.ja: 長く続く制度や慣行を「なぜ変えられないのか」と問いかけるときに使う。a sacred cow と呼ぶと、その扱いが過剰だという話し手の評価がにじむ。There are no sacred cows. は、どんな制度や前提も議論の対象にできるという宣言。
nuance.en: Calling a rule, tradition, or institution a sacred cow usually questions why it gets special protection from scrutiny. There are no sacred cows means that everything can be examined or reconsidered.

en: a taboo: A subject people avoid discussing or a practice they consider forbidden. A sacred cow can be discussed openly while criticism or change is resisted.
a pet project: A project someone is personally attached to. It becomes a sacred cow if others feel they cannot question it.
an article of faith: A belief held with firm conviction. Sacred cow highlights the reluctance to challenge it.
ja: a taboo：話題にすることや行為そのものがタブーとされること。sacred cow は公に語られていても、批判や変更が避けられるものを指す。
a pet project：誰かが特別に力を入れているお気に入りの事業。周囲が異を唱えられなくなれば sacred cow とも言える。
an article of faith：固く信じられている信条。sacred cow は、それに異を唱えにくい点に焦点がある。

note.ja: 手をつけてはいけないものとして扱う、という直接的な言い換え。
note.en: A plain way to describe something protected from challenge or change.

etymology.ja: ヒンドゥー教の伝統で牛が大切にされ、神聖なものとして尊ばれることにちなむ英語の比喩。転じて、批判や見直しの対象から外されるものを指すようになった。
etymology.en: The English idiom alludes to the reverence shown to cows in Hindu traditions. Figuratively, it refers to something treated as exempt from criticism or change.

grammar.countability: countable in a Hail Mary; the Hail Mary can name the prayer

usage.capitalization: Hail Mary is normally capitalized. The Hail Mary names the prayer, while say a Hail Mary means to recite it once.
usage.figurative: A Hail Mary can stand alone for a desperate attempt. It can also modify nouns such as pass, play, or attempt.

en: a traditional Catholic prayer addressed to Mary, also known as the Ave Maria
(American football) a long pass, usually toward the end zone late in a game, with a small chance of being caught
(figurative, chiefly US) a last-ditch attempt with little chance of success
ja: 聖母マリアに向けたカトリックの祈り「アヴェ・マリアの祈り」
（アメフト）試合終盤などに、成功率が低くても得点を狙って投げるロングパス
（比喩・主に米）成功の見込みは薄いが、一か八かで試す最後の手

nuance.ja: 比喩では、時間や手段が残り少なく、成功の見込みも薄いと分かったうえで打つ最後の手を指す。仕事で a Hail Mary attempt と言えば、打開の可能性は低いがやってみる、という響き。throw a Hail Mary はアメフトの実際のプレーにも、仕事などの比喩にも使える。
nuance.en: Figuratively, a Hail Mary is an attempt made when time or options are running out and success looks unlikely. It can convey desperation or admiration for trying anyway. Throw a Hail Mary can refer to an actual pass or an attempt in another setting.

en: a last resort: The option you turn to when others have failed. It may be reliable. A Hail Mary stresses the low odds.
a long shot: Something unlikely to succeed. A Hail Mary often comes late, when few alternatives remain.
a shot in the dark: An attempt or guess with little information. A Hail Mary can be well informed even when the odds are poor.
ja: a last resort：ほかに手がなくなったときの最終手段。成功の見込みが高い場合にも使える。a Hail Mary は成功率の低さを強調する。
a long shot：成功の見込みが薄いこと。a Hail Mary は、残り時間やほかの選択肢が少ない段階での試みによく使う。
a shot in the dark：手がかりがほとんどない状態での推測や試み。a Hail Mary は、状況がよく分かっていても成功率が低いときに使える。

note.ja: 失敗を避けるため、最後の望みをかけた試み。
note.en: A final effort to avert failure.

note.ja: 苦しい状況での一か八かの賭け。
note.en: A risky move made when the situation looks bleak.

etymology.ja: Hail Mary はラテン語 Ave Maria に対応する祈りの冒頭の言葉。アメフトでは、成功を祈るしかないようなプレーを指す比喩になった。この用法は以前からあり、1975年にロジャー・ストーバックが決勝点につながったロングパスをそう呼び、広く知られるようになった。
etymology.en: Hail Mary renders the Latin Ave Maria, the opening of the prayer. In American football it became a name for a desperate play whose success one could only hope or pray for. The sporting expression predates 1975, when Roger Staubach helped popularize it by using it for his game-winning pass.

en: (informal, usually in like herding cats) exceptionally difficult to coordinate because the people involved have different plans or act independently

nuance.ja: まとめ役が苦労している様子を、猫を一つの群れにしようとする姿に重ねた冗談めいた表現。参加者がわざと非協力的でなくても、予定や優先事項がばらばらなら使える。会議の日程調整や、複数のチームが同じ方針で動けるようにする場面によく合う。
nuance.en: The idiom makes light of the organizer’s frustration. It fits situations where people have different schedules or priorities, even if they are all willing to help. It can describe arranging a meeting or getting several teams to work toward the same goal.

en: juggle competing priorities: Balance several demands on your own time or resources. Herding cats highlights the difficulty of getting people or moving parts to act together.
get everyone on the same page: Bring people to a common understanding. Herding cats describes how hard the coordination can be.
an uphill battle: Any task that meets persistent difficulty or resistance. Herding cats points more specifically to the challenge of coordination.
ja: juggle competing priorities：優先事項が競合するなかで、自分の時間や資源をやりくりする。herding cats は人や作業の足並みをそろえる難しさを表す。
get everyone on the same page：全員の認識をそろえる。herding cats は、そこに至るまでの調整の大変さを表す。
an uphill battle：困難や抵抗が続く取り組み全般。herding cats は、ばらばらに動く人や物事をまとめる難しさに焦点がある。

note.ja: 調整が難しいことを直接表す。
note.en: A neutral way to describe a coordination problem.

etymology.ja: herd はここでは「動物を群れにまとめて移動させる」。羊の群れを誘導するように、思い思いに動く猫を一方向へまとめようとする難しさを、人や物事の調整にたとえた表現。初出ははっきりしていない。

patterns: earn your bread and butter by + -ing

usage.spelling: Use spaces in the noun phrase and normally hyphenate the adjective before a noun: This work is our bread and butter. It is our bread-and-butter work.
usage.agreement: When the expression is the subject and refers to a single livelihood or core activity, use a singular verb: Our bread and butter is repair work.

en: (literal) bread served with butter or spread with it
(figurative noun) the work or activity someone relies on for their income, or the core business an organization depends on
(attributive adjective) essential to earning a living or keeping a business going, or directly related to everyday needs

（比喩・名詞句）主な収入源、生活の糧、事業を支える仕事の柱
（名詞の前で形容詞として）収入や事業を支える、日常生活の基本的なニーズに関わる

nuance.ja: Small repairs are our bread and butter. は、小さな修理が安定した収入を支える仕事だという意味。華やかさよりも、日々の暮らしや事業を支える実質的な重要さに焦点がある。bread-and-butter issues なら、賃金や家賃など、暮らしに直結する身近な問題を指す。
nuance.en: Calling something your bread and butter emphasizes that you depend on it for steady income or day-to-day work. It often refers to routine work of real practical importance. Bread-and-butter issues are everyday concerns such as wages or housing costs.

en: make a living: A verb phrase for earning enough to support yourself. Your bread and butter often names the work that provides that income.
mainstay: The principal support of an organization or activity. Its support can be financial or take another form.
cash cow: A product or business that produces substantial, regular profits. Bread and butter can describe routine work you rely on even if its profit margins are modest.
breadwinner: The person who provides most of a household’s income. Bread and butter typically refers to the work or source of income.

etymology.en: The expression draws on bread and butter as simple, everyday food. The image of basic sustenance developed into a metaphor for a livelihood and for practical, everyday necessities.
